quote: Mehrere Ungleichungen lösen z. B. das [-...-] zwischen zwei Kreisen liegende Gebiet reell abbilden. oder das zwischen den Schalen einer Cyklide[?] liegende Gebiet etc.
english: Solve several inequalities, e.g. map really the region lying between two circles, or the region lying between the shells of a cyclide, etc.
topic: Notes on forms (binary, quadratic, ternary cubic) whose discriminant cases can be satisfied rationally, on the rational solution of quadratic inequalities as a mapping of regions, a remark on the nature of definitions, and the start of a note on an everywhere-convergent power series.

triage.modern_statement: The note seems to ask the following. Given a region in R^n cut out by several real polynomial (here quadratic) inequalities, for example the annulus between two circles or the shell between the two sheets of a cyclide, find an explicit real polynomial or rational map, possibly from a Euclidean space R^m, whose image is exactly that region. This would be a 'rational solution' of the inequality system, in the way a rational parametrization solves an equation. In today's terms: decide which semialgebraic sets are polynomial or regular (rational) images of R^m, and construct such maps for specific sets bounded by quadrics. This reading of 'reell abbilden' is my interpretation; the entry is short.
triage.answered_by: Hilbert's specific examples (circular annulus, cyclide shell) are not settled in anything I found. The general question was taken up independently about a century later. J.M. Gamboa posed it at the 1990 Oberwolfach real algebraic geometry seminar: characterize the semialgebraic subsets of R^n that are polynomial images of Euclidean space. It was then studied by J.F. Fernando and J.M. Gamboa ('Polynomial images of R^n', J. Pure Appl. Algebra 179 (2003)) and by Fernando and C. Ueno (open quadrant problem, convex polyhedra and their complements, closed balls). Fernando, Gamboa and Ueno surveyed the area in 'Polynomial, regular and Nash images of Euclidean spaces' (Contemp. Math. 697, 2017). I found no source that links this work to Hilbert's note.

evidence.claim: Gamboa proposed characterizing the semialgebraic subsets of R^n that are polynomial images of Euclidean spaces (1990 Oberwolfach Real Algebraic Geometry seminar).
Fernando and Gamboa, 'Polynomial images of R^n', J. Pure Appl. Algebra 179 (2003) 241–254, studies which semialgebraic sets (e.g. complements R^n \ F) are polynomial images of R^n.
Survey by Fernando, Gamboa and Ueno (Contemp. Math. 697, 2017): images of polynomial, regular and Nash maps are semialgebraic sets, and the paper studies which semialgebraic sets arise this way.
Fernando, Ueno et al., 'On regulous and regular images of Euclidean spaces': regular and regulous (rational-type) images of R^n.
Recent work (2024) on polynomial images of closed balls and on 1-dimensional polynomial/regular/regulous images of balls and spheres shows the area is still active.
Further recent work: one-dimensional polynomial, regular and regulous images of closed balls and spheres (2024).

triage.why: The fragment is short. It is my interpretation, not something a source states, that it means representing a semialgebraic region given by inequalities as the real image of a rational or polynomial map. Under that reading, the closest modern counterpart is the theory of polynomial and regular images of Euclidean spaces. Gamboa posed that question in 1990, and Fernando, Gamboa, Ueno and others have developed it actively from 2003 to 2024. A full characterization remains open. Hilbert's note is not among his published problems (the 23 or the 24th). I found no source that ties it to this later work, and no source that settles his two examples.
